summary: Preserve Bitcoin file-cache headroom during AssumeUTXO background validation
details: Native steady plans transfer memory from balance-history to Bitcoin up to a 50 percent host share, keeping at least 4 GiB for balance-history and staying within the whole-node budget. New native configurations default to a 16 GiB steady cap; existing explicit caps remain unchanged.

Bitcoin dbcache is calculated before transferring extra file-cache headroom; balance-history caches shrink with its allocation. The retained steady budget does not gate chain startup or mining on historical validation and does not trigger a later automatic restart.
The operator handbook explains how container memory pressure can cause RPC timeouts even on an idle host, and how to recalculate existing automatic plans while preserving data.
operator_actions: After installing the updated node kit, stop an existing AssumeUTXO node and run usdb-node set-resource-policy --mode auto --bitcoin-steady-memory-cap 16g before doctor/up. If release activation is also required, recalculate before activate-release.
Confirm actual container limits after restart and observe RPC latency and background progress. Custom caps and manual allocations require individual review.
